title: Ravens Passed a Planning Test Scientists Thought Only Apes Could

scenes.text: Scientists thought only humans and apes could plan ahead.
Then Swedish researchers taught ravens that a tool opens a box of food.
They took the box and tool away. An hour later the ravens chose the right tool about 80 percent of the time.
They also picked tokens for better food later over a snack right now, over 70 percent of the time.
They're choosing for a future they can't see yet.

description:
Scientists thought only humans and apes could plan ahead.
A 2017 study in Science by Lund University researchers found five captive ravens picked the right tool for a future task about 80 percent of the time, and nearly 90 percent after a 17-hour delay. One scientist cautions the birds might just be favoring objects linked to food.
Do you think ravens really plan? Comment below.
first_comment: Hold up: one scientist says they might just like objects tied to food. Planner or not?
